---
title: "Three explanations, one measurement"
date: 2026-11-12
description: "During Milestone 2c, three sessions have explained a GPU failure three ways. Instead of choosing between them, Mads-Peter asks for direct evidence, and one per-iteration run on a V100 decides."
---

The first GPU runs of jaxdft had found that LOBPCG stalls near $10^{-12}$ on
a V100, so every test at the tightest SCF tolerance failed. By the time of
this exchange, three explanations stood side by side. The session that ran
the cluster diagnosis blamed the penalty LOBPCG puts on dropped directions.
The draft of the 2c theory post added that the same happened on the CPU. The
review of that draft, by Claude Science, argued that directions are only
dropped at the first iteration, so the penalty could not be the cause, and
proposed a different failure mode.

Mads-Peter asks for the theory post to carry evidence as direct as possible,
without spending an open-ended effort on it. Claude first notices what the
existing data already says, then writes an instrumented copy of LOBPCG that
records, per iteration, exactly the quantity the explanations disagree about:
whether directions are dropped after the first iteration. It writes down what
each outcome would mean before the job runs. One V100 job decides: the GPU
drops directions at every iteration near convergence, the CPU almost never.
The cluster diagnosis was right about the GPU, the draft was wrong about the
CPU, and the review was right about the CPU only. Checking its own write-up
against the data, Claude also catches and corrects a statement it had just
made.

What came of it: the section "Evidence: per iteration, on both devices" of
the [2c theory post](../theory/02c_eigensolver.qmd), the trajectories in
`reference/gpu_lobpcg_floor/`, and the bounded penalty as the established
fix, confirmed on the V100 in the
[validation document](../validation/02c_eigensolver.qmd).
